title: [SEC6] Good: receivedAt vs sentAt for message timestamps
description:
In app.js createMessageBubble() (line 368), the code uses msg.receivedAt (local server timestamp) for displaying to the user, not msg.sentAt (peer-supplied and untrusted).

This is correct. The sentAt timestamp is provided by the sender and could be:
- Incorrect due to sender's clock skew
- Manipulated by a malicious sender
- Used to create confusion about message ordering

Using receivedAt (the actual time the server received the message) is the right choice for display. It provides the true ordering guarantee and is immune to peer manipulation. This aligns with JMAP's design where receivedAt is canonical.
